final_answer_text:
Both runs completed and metrics confirmed (persisted metrics match run outputs exactly).

## Results

| Vehicle | Plant | Completion time (waypoint reached) | Steps | Propulsion energy |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| vehicle-a-otter | planar3 | 10.1 s | 101 | **5.34 J** |
| vehicle-c-azimuth | coupled6 | 36.8 s | 368 | **8.58 J** |

**vehicle-a-otter (planar3) used less propulsion energy** (5.34 vs. 8.58 — about 36% less).

Notes/caveats:
- Neither run consumed the full 60 s duration — both missions terminated early once the single waypoint (30 m north) was reached (at 10.1 s for the Otter, 36.8 s for the azimuth vehicle), so the energy comparison reflects the actual transit to the waypoint, not a full 60 s of station-keeping/thrust.
- The azimuth vehicle also took much longer to reach the waypoint (3.6x the time), consistent with its higher energy use.
- Validation caveat: vehicle-a-otter/planar3 is "validated" for planar maneuvering. vehicle-c-azimuth/coupled6 is flagged as "allocation-demonstrated-dynamics-unvalidated" — its behavioral dynamics have not been independently validated, so treat its energy/time figures with corresponding caution when drawing conclusions.
